scope: Numerical measure layer only: arbitrary positive real values. Same-kind quantity interfaces and canonical source integration remain unfinished.
key_definition: has_greater_equimultiple_ratio(a,b,c,d) iff there exist m,n in N+ with m*a>n*b and m*c<=n*d. The non-exceeding comparison retains equality.

proof_routes.order_equivalence: Forward multiply witness inequalities by positive measures and cancel m. Reverse use the established rational separating-equimultiples theorem with swapped pairs.
proof_routes.V7_to_V10: Use established exact equivalences to cross-products and positivity to multiply/cancel; covers both clauses and inversion corollary.
proof_routes.V11: Use established equality of quotients, then package back into the original all-integer comparison predicate.
proof_routes.V13: Directly transport the greater comparison across proportionality, retaining the same m,n witness.
proof_routes.VDef4: Native Archimedean bounds applied to b/a and a/b supply positive integer witnesses.

repairs.0014: sqrt(2)>1 was not automatic;0019 proves it by squaring a supposed contrary bound.
repairs.0028: Direct folding missed the intermediate multiple comparison;0029 uses already-proved quotient equivalence, no additional premises.

controls.0015: accepted: second comparison equality is allowed
controls.0016: rejected: equal ratios cannot be strictly greater

proof_liveness_audit.short_theorem_review: V7–V10 are actual source propositions, not new administrative wrappers; their short proofs consume the established ratio equivalence. V13 consumes the exact integer witness directly.
proof_liveness_audit.premise_review: All measure parameters are positive; source equality/strict inequality/ratio premises are used. No unused dimensional or geometric premises added.
proof_liveness_audit.calculation_review: Only scalar cancellation and comparison transport needed; no long coordinate expansion. V11 uses a single quotient chain and existing forward interface.
proof_liveness_audit.scope_boundary: No same-kind quantity model or canonical Book V item is certified by this numerical checkpoint.
